summary: Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for well over 100 nationalities, including the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and most Commonwealth countries, normally for stays of up to six months — while CARICOM nationals move freely and everyone else applies to a High Commission or embassy before traveling.

source.name: Antigua and Barbuda Immigration Department — Visa FAQs

fee.notes: Non-CARICOM nationals; CARICOM nationals pay XCD 150. A processing fee only — it does not guarantee the extension. Apply in person at the Immigration Department in St John's before your entry stamp expires; each extension is for up to three months.

source.name: Antigua and Barbuda Immigration Department — Extensions

conflict.name: Antigua and Barbuda Immigration Department — extension fees

fee.notes: Single applicant. A couple pays USD 2,000 and a family of the applicant plus up to three dependents USD 3,000, with USD 650 for each additional person; fees are non-refundable. Applicants must show remote income and hold medical and travel insurance covering the two years.

source.name: Antigua and Barbuda Nomad Digital Residence — FAQ

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid beyond the date of your return ticket. Visa applicants need a passport valid for at least 6 months from the date they intend to enter, and airlines may apply a six-month rule too, so travel with six months' validity where you can.

source.name: Antigua and Barbuda Immigration Department — Entry and departure requirements

conflict.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Antigua and Barbuda travel advice
conflict.states: passport valid for at least 6 months after the date you arrive

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including after more than 12 hours' transit through an airport in one. No certificate is needed if you fly in directly from Europe, North America or the rest of the Caribbean.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: No official source makes insurance a condition of entry for ordinary visits. The UK government advises adequate travel health insurance: treatment can be expensive and serious cases may need an emergency evacuation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Antigua and Barbuda travel advice (health)

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must hold a return or onward ticket; immigration officers also ask for the address where you are staying and set the length of stay accordingly.

source.name: Antigua and Barbuda Immigration Department — General Visa Information

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must be able to show evidence that they can maintain themselves during their stay, alongside an onward or return ticket and confirmed accommodation. No fixed amount is published.

source.name: Antigua and Barbuda Immigration Department — General Visa Information

declarations.name: ArriveAntigua online arrival form
declarations.text: The authorities advise travelers to complete the ArriveAntigua form online to speed up entry. It is not mandatory, and it can only be filled in on a phone or tablet within 72 hours of travel.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Antigua and Barbuda travel advice (entry requirements)

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could read publishes Antigua and Barbuda's cash-declaration threshold. Declare large sums of cash to Customs on arrival and departure.

notes: Firearms and ammunition are strictly controlled — bringing any into the country without a permit leads to arrest, including for cruise and yacht passengers.
Fresh produce, plants, meat and dairy are restricted to protect local agriculture; declare anything you are carrying.
Drones must be declared and may require permission from the authorities before use.

payments.text: Hotels, restaurants and larger shops take cards, and US dollars are accepted almost everywhere at a rate near EC$2.60 (banks give EC$2.70). Carry small East Caribbean notes for buses, beach bars and market stalls.

safety.text: Antigua and Barbuda is a calm destination for visitors; the usual issues are opportunistic theft from beaches and rental cars, and strong currents on the Atlantic coast. Hurricane season runs from June to November.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Antigua and Barbuda travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April is dry, breezy and reliably sunny. May to November is hotter and wetter, with the hurricane peak from August to October, but far cheaper.

tips.text: You cannot drive on your home license alone — car rental companies issue a temporary Antiguan driving permit (around EC$50) on the spot when you show a valid license. Driving is on the left.
The hurricane season runs from June to November, peaking in August and September. Book flexible fares and take travel insurance that covers weather disruption if you travel then.
Barbuda is a separate island — reached by a short flight or the ferry from St John's, both weather-dependent. Do not plan a same-day return connection to an international flight.
US dollars are accepted island-wide, but change is usually given in East Caribbean dollars. Check which currency a quoted price is in before you pay.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Antigua and Barbuda?
faq.answer: Probably not. Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for more than 100 nationalities, including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, the EU and most Commonwealth countries — visitors are normally admitted for up to six months. CARICOM nationals move freely. Everyone else applies for a visitor visa at an Antigua and Barbuda High Commission, embassy or consulate before traveling.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Antigua and Barbuda without a visa?
faq.answer: Immigration officers grant the length of stay they think your trip needs, up to six months for most visa-free visitors. Ask for what you actually need at the desk — extending later means a trip to the Immigration Department in St John's and a fee.

faq.question: How much passport validity do I need?
faq.answer: Officially your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay. Airlines frequently apply their own six-month rule, so renew if you have less than six months left.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket?
faq.answer: Yes. Visitors are expected to hold a confirmed onward or return ticket and to give an address in Antigua or Barbuda. Both are commonly checked at the immigration desk.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from Antigua and Barbuda?
faq.answer: Yes — the Nomad Digital Residence lets remote workers and their families live in Antigua and Barbuda for up to two years. It costs USD 1,500 for a single applicant, USD 2,000 for a couple and USD 3,000 for a family of up to four (USD 650 for each additional person), and requires proof of remote income plus medical and travel insurance for the full two years. Short visa-free visits do not permit local employment.
